details: plogme is a renamed fork of the Baileys WhatsApp Web library that belongs to the same publisher-controlled family as @crysnovax/baileys (MAL-2026-15917). It ships the identical forced-follow and fingerprint modules: lib/Utils/channel-policy.js (javascript-obfuscator output, sha256 ee0dc4f66c39603e12b014cc09bee260bb80b9bbfe3d2f1428faccf95bebfec3, byte-identical to the file reported in MAL-2026-15917) hardcodes the publisher's WhatsApp newsletter channel 120363423670814885@newsletter in plaintext and a second channel 120363402922206865@newsletter inside a custom-base64 character array, and exports followCrysnovaxTrustedChannels(); lib/Socket/socket.js (sha256 d6ad429de0e0723c2f19e38c197feb28f60e62526bff155a8da26d52353f66c6, also identical to MAL-2026-15917) imports it at lines 15-16 and invokes it from the connection.update handler so the user's own authenticated WhatsApp account silently follows both channels on every successful connection, with a creds.additionalData once-flag and no opt-out. lib/Utils/integrity.js hashes hostname, platform, arch, cpu model and Node version into a machine fingerprint and POSTs it with the package identity to https://bailey.crysnovax.link/api/v1/verify on every socket connect. All four published versions 1.0.0 through 1.0.3 carry the same modules. pkgwarden reviewed the published tarballs with two independent readers; the obfuscated follow module was decoded rather than executed.
